why: Every sentence this project publishes about what it can do, bound to the command that supports it. A claim with no evidence fails the build; a claim whose evidence failed is published as failed. The two accessibility claims stay separate on purpose — there is no field in which an automated result and a manual pass combine into conformance.

claims.claim: Both language catalogs declare the same keys, with no blank value and no key missing from either.
claims.covers: I18N-01, for the strings that go through the catalog — not for the strings that do not yet, which claim `i18n-coverage` reports on.

claims.claim: A missing translation fails rather than rendering the English string or the raw key.
claims.covers: I18N-01. Proven by a pseudo-locale generated from the catalogs at test time.

claims.claim: Every user-facing string in the shipped artifact comes from a catalog.
claims.covers: I18N-01. This is the claim the product does not yet meet: the sweep names each remaining string.

claims.claim: Date, number and unit formatting resolves from configuration or refuses, and plural selection is data.
claims.covers: I18N-01. Proven against Polish (four plural forms) and Arabic (six), not only the German/English pair.

claims.claim: Every focusable element in the shipped artifact has a role and an accessible name, focus stays visible with colour removed, and nothing traps the keyboard.
claims.covers: A11Y-01, for the properties a machine can decide. It does not cover whether a name is meaningful or whether focus order matches reading order for a person.

claims.claim: An automated rule engine reports no violations over every registered surface, with no rule disabled.
claims.covers: A11Y-01, partially. Automated rules decide a minority of the success criteria by construction; a clean run is consistent with an unusable product. The manual half is claim `a11y-manual-pass`.

claims.claim: A person exercised the runtime and designer workflows with assistive technology.
claims.why: No assistive technology can be driven in this environment. A test asserting that something would be announced correctly is asserting a belief, and none was written.
claims.covers: A11Y-01's manual half. Until this is performed, no conformance statement is supportable regardless of what the automated sweep reports.

claims.claim: The 100-, 500- and 2,000-object scenarios build what they declare and complete within recorded budgets.
claims.covers: TEST-01's scenario half. It shows the scenarios are bounded and run; it is not a statement about how many objects the platform supports.

claims.claim: The capacity budgets were measured on representative browser and Home Assistant hardware.
claims.why: This is a shared cloud container with no declared CPU allocation. Every measurement carries that fingerprint, and the budget file records that it supports "scenario-is-bounded" rather than "platform-capacity".
claims.covers: TEST-01's capacity claim. Running the harness with GLT_CAPACITY_HOST set on named hardware is what would satisfy it.

claims.claim: The Node regression suite passes against the built artifact.

claims.covers: TEST-01's Python half. It runs against the vendored Home Assistant, not a live instance.

claims.claim: The browser suites pass against the exact shipped artifact, with the effect ledger clean.
claims.covers: TEST-01's browser half. Every test runs against dist bytes proven identical to the Companion copy.

claims.claim: Authored source, generated card, Companion copy and staged package agree byte for byte.
claims.covers: TEST-01's artifact half, including per-member and per-ZIP checksums.

claims.claim: Every documentation source is present and non-empty, and the site builds byte-identically twice.
claims.covers: The documentation the wiki job copies verbatim, where an empty source silently deletes a page.

claims.claim: The exact staged artifact installs and loads on the pinned minimum and current Home Assistant lanes.
claims.why: The lane runner probes `docker info` across twelve bounded candidates and this container has no Docker engine. Eight phase registers carry the same row with its exact failure output.
claims.covers: TEST-01's compatibility half. Nothing in this repository currently demonstrates the artifact installing on either lane.

claims.claim: Every declared dependency's provenance is verified against its source repository.
claims.why: All five third-party repository endpoints answer 403 with "GitHub access to this repository is not enabled for this session"; api.github.com/rate_limit answers 200, so this is a repository-scope limit rather than a network one. Attaching five third-party repositories with credentials to satisfy a provenance check would be a disproportionate permission change.
claims.covers: TEST-01's supply-chain half. It blocks the Phase-1 gate and every gate recursing into it.
